name: Epsilon Serpentis
description: A naked-eye star 21.6 parsecs away, 1.8 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 141795: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.768 +/- 0.017 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.783 +/- 0.04

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 141795: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.82 +/- 0.026

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 141795: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 8084 +/- 102

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 141795: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 46.28 +/- 0.19 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 22 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.8 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.768 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.783 solar radii and 8,084 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 141795: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
